eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study analyzes adult lung transplant recipients using non‑linear machine learning models (Random Forests) to predict post‑transplant survival, meeting all population, intervention, outcome, and study design criteria.

identification_methods.Setting: Retrospective cohort using national UNOS registry data
identification_methods.Comments: Study evaluated predictive accuracy of LAS and novel models for 1‑year and 3‑year post‑lung transplant mortality using UNOS data.
identification_methods.Institution: University of Washington, Seattle; Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, Baltimore
identification_methods.Address: 1959 NE Pacific Street, Box 356522, Seattle, WA 98107
identification_methods.Dataset Source: UNOS (United Network for Organ Sharing) database via OPTN
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adult patients (≥18 years) receiving first lung transplant between May 1, 2005 and May 1, 2017; excluded lost to follow‑up.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator), Random Forests
identification_methods.Comparator: Lung Allocation Score (LAS) and Chan et al. model
identification_methods.Input Variables: Pre‑transplant recipient covariates from UNOS (e.g., demographics, pulmonary function, labs, diagnosis) and donor covariates in secondary analyses.
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Categorical missing values grouped into a separate category; continuous variables imputed with mean.
identification_methods.Validation Method: Random split: 85% development set, 15% validation set; performance assessed on validation cohort.
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Calibration evaluated by decile plots and calibration slope; models compared using AUC, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV.

population.Inclusion criteria: Adult patients (≥18 years) who had their first lung transplant between May 1, 2005 and May 1, 2017
population.Population Notes: Retrospective cohort from UNOS; data split into 85% development set and 15% validation set
population.Diagnosis: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (most common, 38% of cohort)
population.Pre-transplant Support: Mechanical ventilation (5% alive, 11% died), dialysis prior to transplant (<1% each)

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: LAS, Chan et al model, clinician model (27 a priori predictors), LASSO, Random Forests
interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: UNOS registry pre‑transplant recipient covariates (and donor covariates in secondary analyses)
interventions_outcomes.Number of Predictors: LAS uses many registry variables; clinician model uses 27 pre‑selected predictors; LASSO selected a subset of available UNOS variables (≈15–20 listed)
interventions_outcomes.Feature Selection Method: A priori expert selection for clinician model; LASSO shrinkage for LASSO model; variable importance (Gini) for Random Forests
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Static baseline data at time of transplant
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Random 85% development set, 15% validation set; logistic regression fitted on selected covariates; calibration assessed by decile plots
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: 1‑year mortality (death or re‑transplant), 3‑year mortality, calibration metrics, AUC, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary outcome was death or re‑transplant within the specified timeframe
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: AUC low for all models (0.55–0.62); NPV high (0.87‑0.90); PPV low (<0.25); LAS overestimated risk
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported against: LAS, Chan et al model, clinician model, LASSO, Random Forests
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported as: Area under the receiver‑operator characteristic curve (AUC)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All lung transplant recipients in the validation cohort
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Threshold: Cut‑point maximizing combined sensitivity and specificity (Youden index)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: AUC calculated on a completely held‑out validation set
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: LAS overestimated risk, novel models did not improve prediction; calibration poor for high‑risk patients
